validation.method: Canonical endpoint sweep comparing each App Platform app against its live GCP original. Same path set D-5 used (17 dashboards, 23 api). Three-tier classification: status, byte length, content-type and raw bytes; then CRLF-normalised bytes; then JSON canonicalised with a fixed auditable volatile-key list. Verdicts: MATCH, MATCH-ERR (both sides same non-2xx, identical body), MATCH-~ (equivalent payload, benign difference itemised), DIVERGED (real difference).
validation.vantagePoint: GCP Cloud Build, project smartcity-os-prod. Chosen because this host resets connections to *.ondigitalocean.app; every local attempt failed with 'Recv failure: Connection was reset' while the apps were serving.

theThreeBenigns.reading: gcp 200/138, do 200/139, bodyClass volatile-only, first byte difference at offset 65
theThreeBenigns.whyBenign: Differs only in the keys heapTotalMB, heapUsedMB, timestamp -- a clock and two heap counters from two independent processes. The 1-byte length difference exists because those volatile numbers render with different digit counts (94 vs 99 MB, 99 vs 119 MB).
theThreeBenigns.framing: content-length gcp=138 do=null (App Platform streams chunked)

theThreeBenigns.whyBenign: Differs only in lastScrapeAt and lkgFreshAt, the scraper's own timestamps. Both sides report ok:true, lastScrapeStatus ok, cachedSource municode -- the same functional state at a different moment.

theThreeBenigns.reading: gcp 200/10259, do 200/10259, bodyClass identical -- BODIES IDENTICAL
theThreeBenigns.whyBenign: The payload is byte-identical; the only difference is framing. This is the cleanest illustration of why two tiers was not enough: a naive comparison called a byte-identical response DIVERGED purely because Cloud Run sets Content-Length and App Platform omits it in favour of chunked transfer encoding.

result_api.framingFinding: App Platform omits Content-Length and streams chunked where Cloud Run sets the header explicitly. Measured only on the api's 200s; the dashboards app set Content-Length on all 17. Both are equivalent HTTP; recorded so a future byte-comparison does not flag it.

whatDOsPipelineSaidAtClose_2026-09-17T19.consequenceForTheOperator: Re-verified at 19:34Z: the apex entry is phase ACTIVE with certificate_expires_at at the epoch and ensure-certificate carrying DomainOwnershipVerificationErr, while www is still CONFIGURING with verify-cname RUNNING. The www entry is actively waiting, so it should resolve on its own once the CNAME lands. The apex is the uncertain one: its pipeline already ran to completion and settled, so DO may treat the failed issuance as done rather than retrying. Expect to wait ~15-30 min after the DNS change, then check certificate_expires_at; if it is still the epoch, re-add the apex domain in the app's Domains tab (remove then re-add smartcityos.io) to force a fresh validation run. Stated as a contingency rather than a fact because this lane could not observe a retry: no DNS change was made, so no retry could be provoked.

didTheCertificateValidationActuallyReach.answer: YES, and this is direct evidence of how DO validates the apex.
didTheCertificateValidationActuallyReach.instrument: GCP Cloud Logging, smartcity-os-prod, smartcity-api request logs
didTheCertificateValidationActuallyReach.reading: 19:05:04 and 19:05:03 (x3) -- GET /.well-known/acme-challenge/TiqNzSc_9dyEn7Iznrr__RzaepO6IfLZoRk7EDTuC53QdoVg4GQmfL6lp7DBYO5K with User-Agent 'bushbaby/2026.9.7'; plus the http:// (port 80) form at 19:05:03 (x3).
didTheCertificateValidationActuallyReach.whyItMatters: DO's ACME agent is issuing an HTTP-01 challenge for smartcityos.io. The domain attach was at 19:04:56Z, so these fires are seconds after it and are this lane's doing. The challenge resolves to smartcityos.io, which still points at Google, so it lands on the GCP original -- where no such token exists. That is the DomainCertPendingValidation above, live. It means the apex validates by HTTP-01 via the apex itself, so once the apex A records point at DO's ingress the challenge will reach DO and issuance should complete without a separate TXT record.
didTheCertificateValidationActuallyReach.corroboration: 19:04:59-19:05:00 -- /.well-known/cf-custom-hostname-challenge/7d75dbc4-582a-4c3d-b1b8-ea999488b4a1 with User-Agent 'Cloudflare Custom Hostname Verification', consistent with App Platform's ingress being Cloudflare-fronted (the static ingress IPs 162.159.140.98 / 172.66.0.96 are Cloudflare-owned).

recordsTheOperatorMustCreate.source: DigitalOcean App Platform documentation, read 2026-09-17: the platform publishes two shared static ingress IPs for A records, and for the www host a CNAME to the app's default ingress.
recordsTheOperatorMustCreate.mustRemove: The existing conflicting apex A records 216.239.32.21 / 216.239.34.21 / 216.239.36.21 / 216.239.38.21 (Google ghs.googlehosted.com) and the www CNAME to ghs.googlehosted.com. ALSO the four existing apex AAAA records 2001:4860:4802:32::15 / :34::15 / :36::15 / :38::15 (Google) -- read live at 2026-09-17T19:34Z and NOT flagged in the first cut of this artifact. Leaving them is a silent half-cutover: IPv6-capable clients, which include the iPhone Safari traffic seen in the GCP logs, keep reaching Google while IPv4 reaches DigitalOcean. Replace them with the two AAAA values above, or delete them for an IPv4-only apex; do not leave the Google ones in place. Keep any MX/SPF records untouched.

The A/AAAA values above are the platform's documented shared static ingress IPs; the www CNAME is read directly from this app's default_ingress. If DO's control panel shows a domain-specific value that differs from these, the panel is authoritative.

correction_2026-09-17T20_45Z_READ_THIS_B.why: Everything above was written before the cutover and describes the pre-cutover state. The operator then changed the GoDaddy records by hand and the cutover completed. Two readings in this file were wrong and are corrected here rather than deleted, so the error and its shape remain visible.
correction_2026-09-17T20_45Z_READ_THIS_B.correction1_noCertificateWasWrong: The apex reading said 'certificate_expires_at 1970-01-01 -- NO CERTIFICATE EXISTS'. That inference was wrong in its consequence. Measured from GCP Cloud Build at 20:35Z, smartcityos.io serves a chain-verified, publicly-trusted certificate with CN=smartcityos.io issued by Google Trust Services 'WE1', valid to 2026-12-16T20:30:00Z; www serves the same for CN=www.smartcityos.io. certificate_expires_at tracks DigitalOcean's OWN issuance attempt, which did fail; the certificate actually presented for a Cloudflare-fronted custom hostname is obtained by a different path. The field is not a proxy for what a customer receives.
correction_2026-09-17T20_45Z_READ_THIS_B.correction2_noRetryWasWrong: consequenceForTheOperator said DO 'will not re-attempt issuance until its DNS check sees the records' and offered a remove-and-re-add-the-domain contingency. Both parts were wrong. DO's ACME agent (`bushbaby/2026.9.7`) was observed re-attempting the apex HTTP-01 challenge roughly every 5-11 minutes for 85 minutes -- 19:18, 19:22, 19:27, 19:32, 19:39, 19:46, 19:54, 20:03, 20:14, 20:27, 20:28Z -- so the pipeline never stopped retrying and the contingency was unnecessary. The error was reading a permanent stop into a status field that had merely stopped changing. How to check this class of claim: count the events in the log rather than reading the step status.
correction_2026-09-17T20_45Z_READ_THIS_B.correction3_howTheApexWasActuallyServed: The apex is served over a valid certificate even though DO's ensure-certificate step still carries DomainOwnershipVerificationErr and its certificate_expires_at remains the epoch. A successor must not use either field to judge certificate health for these hostnames. Check the chain from outside.
correction_2026-09-17T20_45Z_READ_THIS_B.outcome: Both hostnames resolve to DigitalOcean, are served by App Platform's Cloudflare-fronted ingress (edge header `server: cloudflare` with a cf-ray, against the original's `server: Google Frontend`), and pass with 0 hard divergences across 23 swept paths each. The GCP original received zero customer requests after 20:32:30Z. See _inbox/2026-09-17_204000_d9_cutover_verification.json and the close's `amendment` field.

scratch.LESSON: A two-tier byte comparison calls a byte-identical response DIVERGED when the only difference is transport framing (Cloud Run sets Content-Length, App Platform streams chunked). Compare payloads, classify framing separately, and record the reason -- otherwise a clean migration reads as a failure.

git's .gitattributes is load-bearing for served bytes: an asset the origin serves as CRLF can be silently rewritten to LF by any checkout. `git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol --numstat` is the check that distinguishes 'line endings only' from real content drift.
scratch.DEAD-END: Validating *.ondigitalocean.app from this host. Every curl and fetch failed with 'Recv failure: Connection was reset' while both apps were demonstrably serving to GCP Cloud Build. Use Cloud Build as the vantage point; do not read a local reset as an app fault.
`doctl compute domain list` / `domain records list` with the agent token: 403. The token is Apps+Droplets only. The DNS values are not readable through this credential.
`doctl apps spec validate --spec <file>`: unknown flag. Pass the path positionally.
scratch.GROUND-TRUTH: As of 2026-09-17T19:12Z, both App Platform apps serve byte-identical to their GCP originals across all 40 swept paths (0 hard divergences), from the pinned commits, and neither carries any customer traffic.

As of 2026-09-17T19:13Z, smartcityos.io still resolves to Google with TTL=600 and GoDaddy nameservers, and the GCP smartcity-api is receiving real browser, crawler and scanner traffic -- not only its uptime checker.

DO is already attempting HTTP-01 validation on the apex every few minutes and will keep failing until then; the DOMAIN_FAILED alert rule is armed on this app.
